/-!
# Asymptotic density of powerful numbers

Let $Q(x)$ denote the number of powerful integers up to $x$. Erdős and Szekeres [ES35] proved
$$Q(x) = \frac{\zeta(3/2)}{\zeta(3)} x^{1/2} + O(x^{1/3}),$$
and Bateman and Grosswald [BG58] sharpened this to
$$Q(x) = \frac{\zeta(3/2)}{\zeta(3)} x^{1/2} + \frac{\zeta(2/3)}{\zeta(2)} x^{1/3} + O(x^{1/6}).$$
Improving the exponent $1/6$ in the error term unconditionally remains open; conditional
improvements are known under the Riemann Hypothesis.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Powerful_number)
- [ES35] Erdős, P. and Szekeres, G., *Über die Anzahl der Abelschen Gruppen gegebener Ordnung
  und über ein verwandtes zahlentheoretisches Problem*, Acta Sci. Math. (Szeged) 7 (1935), 95–102.
- [BG58] Bateman, P. T. and Grosswald, E., *On a theorem of Erdős and Szekeres*,
  Illinois J. Math. 2 (1958), 88–98.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Asymptotics Real

namespace PowerfulNumbersDensity

/-- $Q(x)$ is the number of powerful integers $n$ with $1 \le n \le x$. -/
noncomputable abbrev Q (x : ℝ) : ℕ := {n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ n.Powerful ∧ (n : ℝ) ≤ x}.ncard

/-- The leading constant $\zeta(3/2)/\zeta(3) = 2.173\ldots$ -/
noncomputable abbrev A : ℝ := (riemannZeta (3 / 2)).re / (riemannZeta 3).re

/-- The second-order constant $\zeta(2/3)/\zeta(2)$, where $\zeta(2/3)$ is given by analytic
continuation. -/
noncomputable abbrev B : ℝ := (riemannZeta (2 / 3)).re / (riemannZeta 2).re

/--
Erdős and Szekeres [ES35] proved that the number of powerful integers up to $x$ satisfies
$$Q(x) = \frac{\zeta(3/2)}{\zeta(3)} x^{1/2} + O(x^{1/3}).$$
In particular $Q(x) \sim \frac{\zeta(3/2)}{\zeta(3)} \sqrt{x}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem asymptotic_erdos_szekeres :
    (fun x : ℝ => (Q x : ℝ) - A * x ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2)) =O[atTop]
      fun x => x ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3) := by
  sorry

/--
Bateman and Grosswald [BG58] proved the sharper asymptotic
$$Q(x) = \frac{\zeta(3/2)}{\zeta(3)} x^{1/2} + \frac{\zeta(2/3)}{\zeta(2)} x^{1/3} + O(x^{1/6}).$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem asymptotic_bateman_grosswald :
    (fun x : ℝ => (Q x : ℝ) - A * x ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2) - B * x ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)) =O[atTop]
      fun x => x ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 6) := by
  sorry

/--
Can the exponent $1/6$ in the error term of the Bateman–Grosswald asymptotic be improved
unconditionally? That is, is there $\delta > 0$ such that
$$Q(x) = \frac{\zeta(3/2)}{\zeta(3)} x^{1/2} + \frac{\zeta(2/3)}{\zeta(2)} x^{1/3} +
O(x^{1/6 - \delta})?$$
Improvements are known under the Riemann Hypothesis.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem error_term_improvement :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ δ > (0 : ℝ),
      (fun x : ℝ => (Q x : ℝ) - A * x ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2) - B * x ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)) =O[atTop]
        fun x => x ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 6 - δ) := by
  sorry

end PowerfulNumbersDensity

findings.description: The declaration records only an O(x^(1/6)) remainder, whereas the cited Bateman–Grosswald asymptotic gives o(x^(1/6)), and their Theorem 3 gives an explicit logarithmic saving beyond that. Thus the Lean statement omits the conclusion that the remainder divided by x^(1/6) tends to zero. Big-O and little-o are not equivalent here: the function x^(1/6) itself satisfies the former but not the latter, as checked in Lean. The current statement is a correct weaker corollary and could reasonably be intended as a coarse benchmark for the subsequent open question, so this is a clarification/strength-of-statement concern rather than a false theorem.
findings.source_evidence: Bateman–Grosswald, On a theorem of Erdős and Szekeres (1958), §5, p. 95: “In particular the simple estimate M(n) = o(n), which is equivalent to the prime number theorem, gives an error term o(x^(1/6)).” Theorem 3 gives a stronger exponentially decaying logarithmic factor. Full text read through https://r.jina.ai/https://projecteuclid.org/download/pdf_1/euclid.ijm/1255380836. The Wikipedia-linked Encyclopedia of Mathematics entry explicitly displays N₂(x) = A x^(1/2) + B x^(1/3) + o(x^(1/6)): https://encyclopediaofmath.org/wiki/Power-full_number.
findings.suggested_fix: If this declaration is intended to state the standard Bateman–Grosswald asymptotic, replace `=O[atTop]` with `=o[atTop]` and update the corresponding prose. Alternatively, explicitly identify the current statement as a coarser corollary retained only to establish the exponent benchmark; the original theorem's logarithmic saving could be stated separately.

review.notes: Checked all six declarations. No other mathematical mismatch was found. The scratch file /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors or warnings. It verifies finiteness of the set counted by Q, agreement with finite counts (including Q(0)=0, Q(1)=1, Q(100)=14 and a nonintegral cutoff), the prime-divisor definition on positive integers, positivity of both zeta denominators, the eventual interpretation of big-O, and the equivalence between a global δ>0 and an exponent strictly below 1/6. The known logarithmic savings and recent results with additional zero-residue terms do not settle the file's unconditional fixed power-saving question; no status change is indicated. The reviewed file was left unchanged.
